page: Vultr vhp-2c-4gb-intel is a virtual machine belonging to the High Performance server family. It features an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor with 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core under a shared CPU allocation model. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz and includes 32 KB L1d cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a local 100 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark results indicate moderate single-core performance alongside constraints in multi-core and memory-intensive operations. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score of 1464.88 falls within the average range, and single-threaded gzip compression reaches 24.52 GB/sec. However, multi-core stress-ng performance is weak at 2885.17, reflecting the shared CPU allocation. Memory bandwidth is limited, with large-block read speeds at 18.34 GB/sec and write speeds at 14.91 GB/sec. Database operations under Passmark score 683.09, and Redis SET operations achieve 3.44 million operations per second. Large language model inference on a small 135M model is slow, yielding 137.94 tokens per second for prompt processing and 31.5 tokens per second for text generation.

Given its shared CPU architecture and modest memory capacity, this server type offers an entry-level resource profile suitable for budget-conscious deployments. The inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage provides fast disk access, but the shared CPU allocation and lower memory bandwidth make it less suitable for sustained high-throughput workloads or intensive database operations. Appropriate workloads include lightweight web serving, basic single-threaded application hosting, development environments, and simple background tasks that do not require dedicated CPU resources.
